post.description:
Swap the shared demo user's placeholder handle for a real one, per game.

This router is only mounted when `demo_login_enabled` (main.py), so demo mode
is already enforced. Scoped further to the demo user (`auth_id ==
DEMO_AUTH_ID`) so real users' immutable bindings and the admin-only unlink are
untouched. `rebind` soft-unbinds the old link and binds the new handle — live
host verification + real skill bootstrap — in one transaction, so a bad handle
leaves the old link intact. Returns the same `LinksResponse` as `/links`.
Reset the shared demo account to its fresh-login state (demo user only).

Inject a finished match so a wager can settle without playing one.

The row is written against the target's **linked host account**, and the
adapter merges it into `poll_eligible_games` alongside real history. So the
settlement worker, the pool engine and the payout path all read it through
the same call they use for a real match, and none of them has a branch for
it. That is the point: a demo that proves the real path works.

Settle one pool or tournament now, instead of at its window close.

Runs the worker's own grade-then-settle sequence for a single contest. It
does not shortcut grading: the contest is graded from whatever match history
the adapters return, so a forced settlement still reflects real (or injected)
results rather than a fabricated outcome.

ActionResult.title: ActionResult

AddFriendRequest.title: AddFriendRequest

AdjustRequest.title: AdjustRequest

AdminContestRow.title: AdminContestRow
AdminContestRow.description: A contest the user took part in (unified across match/pool/tournament).

AdminUserSummary.title: AdminUserSummary
AdminUserSummary.description: A row in the users table (search results / list).

ChallengeAcceptResponse.title: ChallengeAcceptResponse
ChallengeAcceptResponse.description: Accepting forms a PENDING match; the client navigates to it to confirm.

ChallengeCreatedResponse.title: ChallengeCreatedResponse
ChallengeCreatedResponse.description: The created challenge, plus the shareable path for invite links.

ChallengePreviewResponse.title: ChallengePreviewResponse
ChallengePreviewResponse.description: Public invite-link preview (no auth) — market, entry, challenger name.

ChallengeView.title: ChallengeView
ChallengeView.description: A challenge as a party sees it (the Respond slip / sent list).

ChatReadResponse.title: ChatReadResponse
ChatReadResponse.description:
Named apart from the notifications mark-read so the two never collide in
the generated OpenAPI component map.

ContestRequest.title: ContestRequest
ContestRequest.description: File a dispute against any contest type (match | pool | tournament).

ConversationView.title: ConversationView
ConversationView.description: A row in the conversation list (and the header of an open thread).

CreateChallengeRequest.title: CreateChallengeRequest
CreateChallengeRequest.description:
One shape for all three flows (the server picks based on which fields are
set): direct (`challengee_id`), rematch (`rematch_of`), or invite link
(neither). game/market/entry are ignored for a rematch (copied from the
original match). Entry is a preset choice — the server owns the cents.

CreateLinkRequest.title: CreateLinkRequest
CreateLinkRequest.description:
Intent to bind a host account. The server fetches + verifies everything;
the client only names the game and the handle to claim.

DemoDepositRequest.title: DemoDepositRequest
DemoDepositRequest.description: Server-defined preset only — never an arbitrary client amount.

DifficultyCard.title: DifficultyCard
DifficultyCard.description: One difficulty quoted from the viewer's own baseline (design PDF p.4).

DisputeView.title: DisputeView
DisputeView.description: A dispute as its filer sees it.

warning.title: Warning
warning.default: Settlement was forced by an admin, not by the contest window.

Forecast.title: Forecast
Forecast.description:
The duel-forecast disclosure for a stat/chess pairing.

`you_win_prob` is `P(you beat opponent)` from the model (held near 0.50 by
the eligibility window); `label` is the honest one-liner for the matched card.

FormatStat.title: FormatStat
FormatStat.description: A single chess time-control's verified stats, sourced from the host.

FriendItem.title: FriendItem
FriendItem.description: One person in the friends list or a pending request (design PDF p.8).

GameLink.title: GameLink
GameLink.description:
One game's row on Profile: linked snapshot or an empty/blocked slot.

`status`: LINKED (active binding), BLOCKED (game flag off or binding frozen),
UNLINKED (available to link), COMING_SOON (in the catalog, no adapter yet).

GettingStarted.title: GettingStarted
GettingStarted.description:
First-match funnel progress — drives the "getting started" checklist that
nudges a new player from signup to their first wager.

GradingExplanation.title: GradingExplanation
GradingExplanation.description:
"Why this result" — the transparent grading record for a contest the
viewer was in: the rule, what each side produced, and the decision.

InviteDraft.title: InviteDraft
InviteDraft.description:
The client's half of an invite card. Entry is a preset choice — the
server validates it against the offered presets and owns the cents.

LinksResponse.title: LinksResponse
LinksResponse.description: Every registered game with the viewer's link state — drives Profile.

MarkReadRequest.title: MarkReadRequest
MarkReadRequest.description: Mark specific notifications read, or all of them when `ids` is omitted.

MarketRow.title: MarketRow
MarketRow.description: One market row on the Play screen (design PDF p.1).

MatchView.title: MatchView
MatchView.description: A match as one participant sees it (design's matched / active slip).

MeResponse.title: MeResponse
MeResponse.description: `/me` payload: the user, a computed onboarding flag, and staking limits.

MessageView.title: MessageView
MessageView.description: One rendered message. `payload` is populated for invite cards only.

OpenConversationRequest.title: OpenConversationRequest
OpenConversationRequest.description:
Open (or reopen) a thread: a friend's `user_id` for a DM, or
`kind='support'` for the support thread.

PoolEnterRequest.title: PoolEnterRequest
PoolEnterRequest.description: Enter a pool = enqueue. Ids + preset only — no bar, no amount.

PoolsListResponse.title: PoolsListResponse
PoolsListResponse.description: The "Open pools" surface: your in-flight rooms + queue state.

ProfileSnapshot.title: ProfileSnapshot
ProfileSnapshot.description:
Verified skill profile for one linked host account.

Chess populates the per-format / `primary_speed` fields; other titles leave
those empty and use the generic `rating` / `rank_label` / `kd` descriptors.
`game` is the adapter id.

QueueRequest.title: QueueRequest
QueueRequest.description: Join the queue. Ids + a server preset only — no amounts, no timestamps.

QueueStatusResponse.title: QueueStatusResponse
QueueStatusResponse.description: Where the viewer stands: idle, searching (band + wait), or matched.

SendMessageRequest.title: SendMessageRequest
SendMessageRequest.description: Either a typed line or an invite card (exactly one of the two).

warning.title: Warning
warning.default: This is an injected result, not a real match. It is indistinguishable from a real one downstream by design.

SteamCallbackRequest.title: SteamCallbackRequest
SteamCallbackRequest.description:
Every `openid.*` parameter Steam put on the return URL, unmodified.

They are forwarded to Steam verbatim for verification, so the client must
not filter or reorder them.

UpdateFlagRequest.title: UpdateFlagRequest
UpdateFlagRequest.description:
Patch a flag: toggle `enabled` and/or replace its `payload` (e.g.
`geo_config`'s excluded-state list). At least one field must be present.

active_games.title: Active Games

UpdateMeRequest.title: UpdateMeRequest
UpdateMeRequest.description:
Onboarding (username + state + 18+, set once) and/or limit edits.

All fields optional so the endpoint serves both onboarding and later limit
changes. Lowering a cap is instant; raising is delayed (see limits_service).

WaitingRow.title: WaitingRow
